az_carnivore_pinnacle_lappy_mcdome.blurb: Two small walls tucked beside a gully near the Sheepshead dome, in the west part of the Dragoon Mountains in southern Arizona. Six routes split evenly between sport and trad, most of them two pitches. Grades start in the high 5.7s, cluster between 5.8 and 5.10, and top out with one 5.13. The rocks are hidden from the base of the dome, so they see little traffic and make a quieter fallback when the main dome is busy. Plan on a long approach of about 45 minutes that involves a fifth-class scramble up the gully.

az_cowpunks_wall.blurb: A steep, overhanging buttress right beside the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, in the Windy Ridge zone above Tucson. Six routes: five sport and one trad, running from 5.10 to the 5.13 range, with most falling around 5.11. Expect some holdless stretches and crumbly, loose rock in places. The wall is warm and sunny in winter, goes into shade around midday, and its base stays shaded later in the afternoon. The walk from the road is only a few minutes of scrambling down a dirt slope and crossing scree.

az_gallery_the.blurb: A small cluster of bolted routes in a gully on Mount Lemmon, within the Windy Point West zone along the Catalina Highway. All six lines are sport climbs, and they are hard: one around 5.11, one 5.12 and four in the 5.13 range. The main wall is steep by Lemmon standards, and the routes stay shaded for most of the day. Few of the lines see much traffic, so crowds are unlikely. Reaching the belay takes some scrambling, either by rappelling into the gully or hiking down and back up between the fins.

az_monkey_skull.blurb: A tiny bouldering patch on Panther Peak, on the west side of the Tucson Mountains. It sits roughly 100 feet downhill from the bigger Beast boulder: two blocks with a small chimney between them, the left one carrying a bulging overhang that resembles a skull from a distance. Six problems, all short of the hard end: one easy, three at V2 and two at V3. The rock is volcanic conglomerate with pebbles from pea to beach-ball size, and quality across Panther ranges from very good to crumbly. Getting in from the trailhead is a hike of about 45 minutes.
